# MEMORANDUM

**TO:** Supervising Partner
**FROM:** Associate
**DATE:** October 18, 2026
**RE:** Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc. / Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC: Review of Provider Drafts (MSA, SOW No. 1, DPA) Against the Signed Term Sheet
**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL | ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

---

## I. Summary

I reviewed the five documents in the matter folder, both individually and against each other:

- the Master Services Agreement draft (**MSA**), Effective Date January 1, 2027, with a 2-year Initial Term (§ 14.1);
- Statement of Work No. 1 (**SOW**), Start Date January 15, 2027, with a Monthly Service Fee of $184,500 (§§ 2.1, 5.1);
- the Data Processing Addendum (**DPA**);
- the signed non-binding Term Sheet dated September 22, 2026; and
- the Quillmore Insurance Brokers cover letter enclosing Bellweather's certificate of insurance.

Bellweather prepared all three operative drafts. On several points they depart from the Term Sheet and from customer-protective market norms.

Five issues need to be pushed back on in the next turn. They are listed below **in order of importance**:

1. **Overbroad exclusivity (MSA § 3.2).** The clause covers all logistics services nationwide. The Term Sheet limited exclusivity to NYC-metro last-mile home delivery.
2. **One-sided uncapped indemnity (MSA § 11.3).** Harrowgate's broad § 10.2 indemnity is unlimited. Bellweather's indemnity stays capped.
3. **Delaware law and forum in the DPA (DPA § 9.1).** Because of the MSA's order-of-precedence clause, this provision controls over the MSA's New York choice for data disputes.
4. **Three-year auto-renewal with a 15-day opt-out window (MSA § 14.2).**
5. **Unrestricted assignment by Provider (SOW § 8.2).** The MSA assignment clause (§ 17.4) restricts only Harrowgate.

These issues compound each other. Take the worst case: Harrowgate misses the 15-day renewal window. It is then locked into a nationwide exclusive arrangement for three more years. Bellweather could assign that arrangement to an unvetted carrier or a competitor. Throughout that period Harrowgate would carry unlimited indemnity exposure, and any data-incident dispute would go to Delaware.

Section IV lists secondary points. Section V lists items to **raise with the client before the next turn of the draft**.

### Two structural facts that drive the analysis

- **Order of precedence (MSA § 2.3).** If the documents conflict, the **Data Processing Addendum prevails over the MSA, and the MSA prevails over the SOW**. This ranking is what lets the DPA's Delaware clause override the MSA. It also means the SOW's assignment clause is controlled only where the MSA actually conflicts with it, and here the MSA is silent.
- **General liability cap (MSA § 11.1).** Each Party's aggregate liability is capped at **the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim**. At the SOW No. 1 run rate, that is roughly $2.2 million ($184,500 × 12). It will be less for any claim arising early in the relationship.

---

## II. Issues in Order of Importance

### Issue 1: Exclusivity far exceeds the Term Sheet

**Where:** MSA § 3.2 (Exclusivity). Compare Term Sheet § 4.1–4.2, MSA § 14.2 (renewal) and SOW § 4.1 (Service Area).

**What it says:** Bellweather would be Harrowgate's "**exclusive provider** of all warehousing, freight transportation and delivery services required by Customer and its Affiliates **throughout the United States**." Harrowgate and its Affiliates also could not use any third party for those services, or **perform them itself**, anywhere in the U.S.

**Why it matters:**

- **It contradicts the Term Sheet.** Term Sheet § 4.1 limits exclusivity to "last-mile home delivery within the New York City metropolitan area only." Section 4.2 expressly preserves Harrowgate's freedom to use other providers, or to self-perform, for "all warehousing, freight transportation, line-haul and delivery services outside the scope of Section 4.1." The draft clause is far broader than what the parties agreed.
- **The Term Sheet will not protect us.** It is non-binding apart from § 12.2. Once the MSA is signed, its integration and amendment provisions will govern, and the Term Sheet will have no legal effect on this point. We must fix the clause in the MSA itself.
- **It reaches beyond what Bellweather even offers.** SOW § 1.3 puts line-haul outside the Service Area out of scope. Bellweather does not offer those services, yet Harrowgate would be barred from buying them from anyone else.
- **It would put Harrowgate in breach on day one.** The clause bars self-performance and binds Affiliates, so it would sweep in Harrowgate's own trucks, its store-to-store transfers, and any existing carrier or 3PL contracts outside the NYC metro area. SOW § 2.2 refers to Harrowgate's "current facility," which suggests existing arrangements that could breach § 3.2 as of January 1, 2027.
- **The lock-in grows with the renewal term.** Under § 14.2, nationwide exclusivity could extend in three-year increments.

**Recommended fix:** Replace § 3.2 with:

> "3.2 **Exclusivity.** During the Term, and subject to Provider's continued compliance with this Agreement and the Service Levels, Customer shall engage Provider on an exclusive basis for last-mile home delivery of Customer Goods to end customers located within the Service Area defined in Statement of Work No. 1 (the "**Exclusive Services**"). No other services are subject to exclusivity. Customer and its Affiliates remain free to use other providers, or to perform services themselves, for all warehousing, freight transportation, line-haul and delivery services other than the Exclusive Services. Exclusivity shall not apply to (a) deliveries Provider declines, cannot perform within the scheduled window, or cannot perform because of a force majeure event; (b) customer pick-up, store-fleet deliveries or vendor drop-ship; or (c) any period during which Provider is in material breach or has failed the On-Time Delivery Service Level in two consecutive months."

Points to note on this language:

- Anchoring "NYC metropolitan area" to the SOW § 4.1 Service Area gives the term a defined boundary. That Service Area includes four New Jersey counties and Long Island, Westchester and Rockland. The client needs to confirm that scope (see Section V).
- The performance-based release protects Harrowgate if service deteriorates. It should be coordinated with MSA § 17.2, which already allows substitute services after 15 days of force majeure.

---

### Issue 2: Harrowgate's indemnity is uncapped while Bellweather's is capped

**Where:** MSA § 11.3 (Exceptions), read with §§ 10.1, 10.2, 11.1 and 11.2.

**What it says:** "The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to Customer's obligations under Section 10.2, which shall apply **without limitation**." Bellweather's indemnity under § 10.1 gets no matching carve-out. It therefore remains subject to the 12-month fee cap in § 11.1 and to the consequential-damages exclusion in § 11.2.

**Why it matters:**

- **Harrowgate's exposure is unlimited and one-sided.** Section 10.2 is very broad. It covers any third-party claim "arising out of or relating to" (a) Customer Goods, including product defect and IP claims, (b) any Customer **or end-customer** premises where Bellweather performs Services, or (c) "Customer's use of the Services."
- **It is not fault-based.** On its face, § 10.2 could require Harrowgate to indemnify Bellweather for claims caused by Bellweather's own crews. Examples include an in-home injury during a white-glove assembly, or property damage at an end customer's residence. Claims of this kind are the core risk of last-mile delivery.
- **It lifts the consequential-damages exclusion too.** Because § 11.3 also removes § 11.2 for Harrowgate's obligations, Harrowgate could owe Bellweather's lost profits and consequential losses on those claims.
- **Bellweather's protection is thin by comparison.** Its negligence indemnity under § 10.1 is capped at roughly $2.2 million or less, and it has no data-breach indemnity at all.
- **The Term Sheet does not support this.** Term Sheet § 8.1 contemplates a mutual cap "subject to customary exceptions." An uncapped, non-fault customer indemnity is not a customary exception.

**Recommended fix:**

1. **Strike the first sentence of § 11.3.** Then make the exceptions mutual:

> "11.3 **Exceptions.** The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to (a) either Party's indemnification obligations under Section 10 with respect to third-party claims for bodily injury, death or damage to tangible property; (b) either Party's liability for fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct; (c) Provider's obligations under the Data Processing Addendum and Section 9, which shall be subject to a separate cap equal to the greater of [three (3)] times the Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and $[●]; or (d) Customer's obligation to pay Fees properly due."

2. **Narrow § 10.2 to fault.** Insert "to the extent caused by" Harrowgate's breach, negligence or willful misconduct, or by defects in Customer Goods not caused by Provider. Delete clause (c), "Customer's use of the Services." Add: "except to the extent arising from the negligence, willful misconduct or breach of Provider or its personnel or subcontractors."

3. **Expand § 10.1.** Add Bellweather indemnities for Security Incidents and breach of the DPA or § 9, and for subcontractor claims.

4. **Clarify the § 11.1 cap.** Specify "the Fees paid or payable **by Customer under this Agreement and all Statements of Work**." Add a floor (for example, the greater of 12 months' Fees and $[●]) so early-term claims are not capped at a nominal amount.

---

### Issue 3: The DPA's Delaware law and forum controls data disputes over the MSA's New York choice

**Where:** DPA § 9.1. Compare MSA § 18.1, MSA § 2.3 (Order of Precedence) and Term Sheet § 11.

**What it says:** The DPA, and "any dispute ... relating to the Processing of Personal Data or any Security Incident," is governed by "the **laws of the State of Delaware**." The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of courts in "**Wilmington, Delaware**." MSA § 18.1 selects New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County.

**Why it matters:**

- **The DPA controls, not the MSA.** Under MSA § 2.3, the **Data Processing Addendum prevails** over the MSA in any conflict. The two exclusive-forum clauses directly conflict, so for data-related disputes the **Delaware clause controls**. The documents are not consistent on governing law, and we cannot rely on MSA § 18.1 to fix the problem.
- **Disputes will split.** A single Security Incident could generate:
  - a DPA claim, such as breach-response cost reimbursement under DPA § 5.5, that must be brought in Wilmington under Delaware law; and
  - related MSA claims, such as indemnity, loss of Customer Goods data or termination for breach, that belong in New York County under New York law.
- **The result is duplicated cost and inconsistent outcomes.** Parallel proceedings, inconsistent results and a fight over which clause governs any given claim are all likely.
- **Protections drop away.** The DPA has no jury waiver or escalation step corresponding to MSA §§ 18.2–18.4.
- **There is no apparent Delaware connection.** Harrowgate is a New York corporation. The Facility is in New Jersey and the Service Area is NY/NJ. The DPA itself benchmarks safeguards to N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 899-bb (DPA § 4.1).
- **The Term Sheet called for New York.** Term Sheet § 11 provides that all Definitive Agreements, expressly including the DPA (§ 2.1), will be governed by New York law in New York County courts.

**Recommended fix:**

1. Replace DPA § 9.1 with:

> "9.1 **Governing Law and Forum.** This DPA and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, including any dispute relating to the Processing of Personal Data or any Security Incident, shall be governed by Section 18 of the Agreement, including its choice of New York law, exclusive New York County forum, escalation procedure and jury waiver, which are incorporated by reference."

2. Amend MSA § 2.3 so the DPA prevails only "with respect to the Processing and protection of Personal Data." Add: "notwithstanding the foregoing, Sections 11 and 18 of this Agreement shall control over any conflicting provision of the DPA or any Statement of Work." This keeps a provider-drafted ancillary document from overriding core commercial terms in the future.

---

### Issue 4: Three-year automatic renewal with a 15-day opt-out window

**Where:** MSA § 14.2 (Renewal), read with § 14.1 and § 3.2.

**What it says:** After the 2-year Initial Term, the MSA "shall automatically renew for **successive renewal terms of three (3) years** each." The renewal happens unless non-renewal notice is delivered "during the **fifteen (15) day period** ending one hundred twenty (120) days before the expiry." Notice given at any other time "shall be of no effect."

**Why it matters:**

- **The window is very narrow.** For the Initial Term ending January 1, 2029, the window runs approximately August 19 to September 3, 2028. Notice given even one day early or late is void.
- **The renewal term is longer than the Initial Term.** A missed window locks Harrowgate in for three more years. Under the current § 3.2, that means three more years of nationwide exclusivity.
- **There is no exit right.** The MSA has no termination-for-convenience right. SOW § 2.3 ties the SOW to the MSA term, so the SOW renews as well.
- **The Term Sheet left renewal open.** Term Sheet § 10.2 says renewal terms are "to be negotiated." Nothing in the Term Sheet supports this structure.
- **There may be enforcement arguments, but we should not rely on them.** New York's automatic renewal statute, Gen. Oblig. Law § 5-903, requires the service provider to send a reminder notice before the opt-out date. Whether it applies to this logistics arrangement is uncertain. We should not rely on it and should fix the clause contractually.

**Recommended fix:** Replace § 14.2 with:

> "14.2 **Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive renewal terms of one (1) year each (each, a "**Renewal Term**"), unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at any time at least ninety (90) days before the expiry of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term. Provider shall give Customer written notice of the upcoming renewal date not less than one hundred twenty (120) nor more than one hundred eighty (180) days before each expiry."

Also add a Customer **termination-for-convenience** right on 120–180 days' notice during any Renewal Term. If Bellweather resists, consider a termination-for-convenience right with a modest fee during the Initial Term.

---

### Issue 5: Provider can assign freely; only Harrowgate is restricted

**Where:** SOW § 8.2 (Assignment by Provider). Compare MSA § 17.4 (Assignment) and MSA § 2.3.

**What it says:** "**Provider may assign**, delegate or otherwise transfer this SOW, and any of its rights and obligations under this SOW **and under the Agreement**, in whole or in part, to any third party, **without Customer's consent**." Bellweather need only notify Harrowgate within 30 days *after* the assignment takes effect. MSA § 17.4 bars assignment by Customer without Provider's consent, including by merger or change of control, but says nothing about Provider.

**Why it matters:**

- **Nothing in the higher-ranking documents limits Bellweather.** Section 17.4 is silent on Provider, so arguably there is no "conflict" for MSA § 2.3 to resolve. SOW § 8.2 therefore operates as written, and it reaches up into the MSA itself.
- **Harrowgate's most sensitive assets could move without its consent.** Bellweather could transfer the exclusive relationship, Harrowgate's inventory and its end-customer data to an unvetted carrier or to a **Harrowgate competitor** or a competitor's affiliate. Partial assignments could split responsibility for a single operation.
- **It undercuts protections elsewhere in the drafts.** The subcontractor consent requirements in MSA § 7.2, SOW § 8.1 and DPA § 6.1 can be circumvented by assigning instead of subcontracting.
- **Harrowgate is restricted even in the ordinary course.** It cannot assign even in a corporate reorganization or sale without Bellweather's consent.

**Recommended fix:**

1. **Delete SOW § 8.2.**
2. **Make MSA § 17.4 mutual:**

> "17.4 **Assignment.** Neither Party shall assign, delegate or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any Statement of Work, or any of its rights or obligations under them, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, by merger or change of control or otherwise, without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld; provided that (a) either Party may assign this Agreement in its entirety, on written notice, to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, if the assignee assumes all obligations in writing; and (b) it shall be reasonable for Customer to withhold consent to any assignment by Provider to a Customer Competitor. "**Customer Competitor**" means any retailer of furniture or housewares or any Affiliate of such a retailer. No Statement of Work may be assigned separately from this Agreement. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 17.4 is void."

3. **Add a change-of-control termination right.** Harrowgate may terminate without penalty on 60 days' notice within 180 days after a change of control of Provider, or after any permitted assignment by Provider. Exclusivity should fall away automatically on that event.
4. **Add to the DPA** that any assignee must agree in writing to be bound by the DPA before receiving Personal Data.

---

## III. The Insurance Certificate Cover Letter (No Material Issue)

The Quillmore letter is informational. It does not affect contract terms. Its own terms state that the certificate does not amend or extend coverage (§ 5.1). On its face, each listed limit meets MSA § 12.1, and the additional-insured and 30-day cancellation-notice requirements of § 12.2 are addressed. Housekeeping follow-ups:

- **Additional-insured endorsements.** The endorsements are not yet issued; Quillmore says they will be issued "on execution" (§ 3.1). Request copies before the Start Date. Consider making their delivery a condition to go-live in SOW Schedule A, which currently targets January 11, 2027 for certificates.
- **Policy expiry.** The policies expire **July 1, 2027**, six months into the term. Calendar the delivery of renewal certificates.
- **Cyber coverage.** The cyber policy is **claims-made**. MSA § 12.1 should require a retroactive date no later than the Effective Date and a tail or extended reporting period of at least the one-year post-term period.
- **Coverage amounts.** Consider whether the $250,000-per-vehicle motor truck cargo limit is adequate for white-glove furniture loads, and whether additional-insured status should extend to the warehouse legal liability policy.
- **Coverage scope.** Bellweather's coverage does not help Harrowgate with its own § 10.2 indemnity exposure (Issue 2).

---

## IV. Secondary Points for the Next Turn

1. **Customer data return.** MSA § 8.5 and DPA § 8 should allow a Harrowgate-directed transfer of Customer Data to a successor provider during the 90-day transition, not only a return within 30 days.
2. **Service credits.** SOW § 6.2 caps credits at 10% of the monthly fee. Add a chronic-failure termination right, for example missing the same Service Level in 3 of any 6 months.
3. **Force majeure.** In MSA § 17.2, add a Customer termination right if the force majeure event continues beyond 30 days. Suspend Fees for services not performed during it.
4. **Order of precedence.** Beyond Issue 3, provide that a SOW may expressly override the MSA only by reference to the specific MSA section. This would prevent another SOW § 8.2-type provision.
5. **Definition of "Term" (MSA § 1.9).** The definition cross-refers only to § 14.2. Conform it once renewal is revised.
6. **DPA Annex 3 (approved Subprocessors).** The annex is blank. Require it to be completed and approved before the Start Date, consistent with the annex note.

---

## V. Items to Raise with the Client Before the Next Turn

1. **Exclusivity scope.** Confirm that Harrowgate intends exclusivity only for NYC-metro last-mile home delivery, per Term Sheet § 4.1. Confirm that the SOW § 4.1 Service Area, which includes Long Island, Westchester, Rockland and four NJ counties, is the right definition of "NYC metropolitan area." Identify any existing carrier, 3PL, own-fleet or warehousing arrangements, including the "current facility" referenced in SOW § 2.2, that § 3.2 as drafted would breach on January 1, 2027.
2. **Risk tolerance on indemnity.** Ask what product liability and general liability insurance Harrowgate carries, and whether it would accept any uncapped exposure. A mutual, fault-based indemnity for bodily injury and property damage is our recommended position. Obtain a target figure for the data super-cap.
3. **Renewal and exit.** Ask what term flexibility the business wants (1-year renewals, a termination-for-convenience right, any appetite for a termination fee). Confirm who will own the renewal calendar.
4. **Assignment and competitors.** Ask which entities Harrowgate considers competitors for the carve-out. Ask whether Harrowgate anticipates any reorganization or sale that requires its own assignment flexibility.
5. **Delaware.** Confirm that Harrowgate has no business reason to accept Delaware law or forum for data disputes. We recommend insisting on New York, per Term Sheet § 11.
6. **Negotiation posture.** All five issues either depart from the Term Sheet (Issues 1 and 3) or address points the Term Sheet left "to be negotiated" (Issues 2, 4 and 5). Confirm the client is comfortable with us framing Issues 1 and 3 to Bellweather as conformity corrections rather than new asks.
7. **Insurance.** Confirm whether Harrowgate's risk team wants higher cargo or cyber limits before go-live.

Once the client responds, I can prepare a full redline of the MSA, SOW and DPA reflecting the fixes above.

MEMORANDUM

**TO:** Supervising Partner
**FROM:** Associate
**DATE:** October 18, 2026
**RE:** Harrowgate Home Goods, Inc. / Bellweather Freight Logistics LLC: review of provider drafts (MSA, SOW No. 1, DPA) against the signed term sheet and the broker's insurance letter

---

## I. Executive Summary

I reviewed the five documents in the matter folder, both on their own and against each other:

- Master Services Agreement draft (MSA)
- Statement of Work No. 1 (SOW)
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA)
- Signed non-binding term sheet dated September 22, 2026 (Term Sheet)
- Quillmore Insurance Brokers cover letter enclosing a certificate of insurance

Bellweather prepared the initial drafts (Term Sheet § 2.2). In several important places those drafts depart from what the parties agreed in the Term Sheet. Elsewhere they depart from customer-protective norms for a third-party logistics arrangement.

Four issues stand out. They are listed in order of importance below.

1. **Overbroad exclusivity (MSA § 3.2).** The draft makes Bellweather Harrowgate's exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight and delivery services *throughout the United States*. The Term Sheet limited exclusivity to last-mile home delivery in the NYC metro area.
2. **One-sided uncapped indemnity (MSA § 11.3).** Harrowgate's broad § 10.2 indemnity is carved out of both the liability cap and the consequential-damages exclusion. Bellweather's § 10.1 indemnity stays capped at 12 months' fees.
3. **Governing law and forum conflict (DPA § 9.1).** The DPA selects Delaware law and Wilmington courts. Because the DPA outranks the MSA under MSA § 2.3, Delaware would control data-related disputes. This departs from the Term Sheet's New York choice.
4. **Automatic renewal lock-in (MSA § 14.2).** The MSA renews automatically for 3-year terms unless notice is given within a 15-day window. Combined with item 1, a missed date would bind Harrowgate to nationwide exclusivity for three more years.

Several secondary items follow in Part III. Client questions are collected in Part IV.

---

## II. Priority Issues (in order of importance)

### Issue 1: Exclusivity is far broader than the Term Sheet

**Where:** MSA § 3.2 (Exclusivity). Compare Term Sheet §§ 4.1–4.2 and SOW §§ 1.3 and 4.1.

**What it says:**

- MSA § 3.2 appoints Bellweather as Harrowgate's "exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight transportation and delivery services required by Customer and its Affiliates throughout the United States."
- It also bars Harrowgate and its Affiliates from using any third party for, or self-performing, any such services anywhere in the United States.

**What was agreed:**

- Term Sheet § 4.1 provides for exclusivity "for last-mile home delivery within the New York City metropolitan area only."
- Term Sheet § 4.2 states that "No other services are subject to exclusivity." It confirms that Harrowgate remains free to use other providers, or to self-perform, for all warehousing, freight transportation, line-haul and delivery services outside that scope.

**Why it matters:**

- **Nationwide reach.** The clause would prevent Harrowgate from using any other warehouse, carrier, line-haul provider or parcel service anywhere in the country. That would include any existing vendor relationships.
- **Self-performance barred.** It would also stop Harrowgate from running its own fleet or store-to-door deliveries. Because it extends to Affiliates, it reaches the whole corporate group.
- **No matching commitment from Bellweather.** The SOW covers only one New Jersey facility (SOW § 3.1) and a defined NY/NJ Service Area (SOW § 4.1). SOW § 1.3 expressly puts line-haul outside the Service Area out of scope. So Bellweather would hold an exclusive right to services it has not agreed to perform, at prices that have not been set.
- **Possible breach on day one.** Unless Harrowgate's current logistics outside the NYC metro area are wound down by January 1, 2027, Harrowgate could be in breach immediately.
- **Status of the Term Sheet.** The Term Sheet is non-binding (§ 12.1), so it does not itself constrain the definitive agreement. It is, however, strong negotiating leverage. This is a straightforward departure from an agreed term, and we should present it to Bellweather that way.

**Recommended fix:** Replace § 3.2 with language tracking the Term Sheet:

> **3.2 Exclusivity.** During the Term, Customer shall engage Provider on an exclusive basis for last-mile home delivery of Customer Goods to Customer's end customers within the Service Area defined in Statement of Work No. 1 (the "**Exclusive Services**"). Nothing in this Agreement restricts Customer or its Affiliates from engaging any third party to perform, or from performing themselves, (a) any warehousing, fulfillment, freight transportation, line-haul or delivery services other than the Exclusive Services, or (b) any services outside the Service Area. Exclusivity shall not apply to (i) deliveries Customer performs using its own employees and vehicles from its retail stores, (ii) small-parcel shipments tendered to national parcel carriers, or (iii) any period during which Customer is entitled to procure substitute services under Section 17.2 or Provider is in uncured material breach of the service levels in the applicable Statement of Work.

Also consider adding the following:

- A **performance-based release** from exclusivity. For example, Harrowgate could move delivery volume to another carrier if Bellweather misses the on-time-delivery SLA in SOW § 6.1 for two consecutive months, or for any three months in a rolling twelve.
- Language confirming that **exclusivity ends** on any termination or non-renewal.

---

### Issue 2: Harrowgate's indemnity is uncapped while Bellweather's is capped

**Where:** MSA §§ 11.3, 11.1, 11.2, 10.1 and 10.2.

**What it says:**

- **The general cap (§ 11.1).** Each party's aggregate liability is capped at "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim." At the base Monthly Service Fee of $184,500 (SOW § 5.1), that is roughly $2.2 million, before excess-volume charges.
- **Harrowgate's carve-out (§ 11.3).** Both the § 11.1 cap and the § 11.2 exclusion of consequential damages "shall not apply to Customer's obligations under Section 10.2, which shall apply without limitation."
- **No matching carve-out for Bellweather.** There is no corresponding carve-out for Bellweather's indemnity under § 10.1, which therefore remains subject to the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages exclusion.
- **Scope of Harrowgate's indemnity (§ 10.2).** It is very broad. It covers any third-party claim "arising out of or relating to":
  - Customer Goods, including product defect, safety or IP claims;
  - any Customer premises or *end-customer premises* where Bellweather performs Services; or
  - "Customer's use of the Services."
- **No fault limitation.** Section 10.2 has no comparative-fault qualifier and no exclusion for claims caused by Bellweather's own negligence.

**Why it matters:**

- **Unlimited exposure for Bellweather's own conduct.** Read together, these provisions make Harrowgate the unlimited backstop for a wide range of claims. Many of them arise from Bellweather's conduct. Examples include a delivery crew injuring someone inside an end customer's home, damaging the residence, or causing a vehicle accident en route. Each of these "relates to" end-customer premises and to "Customer's use of the Services."
- **Reversal of the agreed risk position.** Bellweather would point to § 10.2 and seek unlimited defense and indemnity. Meanwhile, Bellweather's own § 10.1 indemnity for its negligence, legal violations and employment claims is capped at about $2.2 million. That inverts the risk allocation the parties contemplated.
- **Not a "customary exception."** Term Sheet § 8.1 called for a mutual 12-month-fee cap "subject to customary exceptions." A one-way, unlimited customer indemnity is not a customary exception.
- **Consequential damages also exposed.** Because the carve-out also displaces § 11.2, Harrowgate would be exposed to Bellweather's lost profits and consequential losses on any such claim.
- **Enforceability is a fallback, not a strategy.** Under New York law, an agreement to indemnify a party for its own negligence must be expressed in unmistakably clear terms. Section 10.2 does not say this expressly, which gives us an argument. In the construction context, General Obligations Law § 5-322.1 may also be relevant if any work at end-customer premises were characterized that way. We should not rely on either point. We should fix the drafting.

**Recommended fix:** Pursue three changes, in order of preference.

1. **Delete the first sentence of § 11.3.** Keep the mutual exceptions for fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct and payment of Fees.

2. **If Bellweather insists on uncapped indemnities, make them mutual.** Proposed language:

   > **11.3 Exceptions.** The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to (a) either Party's obligations under Section 10 with respect to third-party claims for bodily injury, death or damage to real or tangible personal property, (b) either Party's liability for fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct, (c) Provider's breach of Section 8, Section 9 or the Data Processing Addendum, which shall be subject to the separate cap in Section 11.4, or (d) Customer's obligation to pay Fees properly due.

3. **Narrow § 10.2 regardless of which option is adopted:**
   - limit item (b) to conditions of the premises not caused by Bellweather;
   - delete item (c) ("Customer's use of the Services") or limit it to Harrowgate's breach of the Agreement;
   - add this sentence: "Customer shall have no obligation under this Section 10.2 to the extent a claim arises from the negligence, willful misconduct or breach of this Agreement of Provider, its personnel or subcontractors."

---

### Issue 3: The DPA's Delaware law and forum override the MSA's New York choice for data disputes

**Where:** DPA § 9.1. Compare MSA §§ 18.1 and 2.3, DPA preamble ("This DPA forms part of the Agreement"), and Term Sheet § 11.

**What it says:**

- **DPA § 9.1** provides that the DPA "and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, including any dispute relating to the Processing of Personal Data or any Security Incident" is governed by "the laws of the State of Delaware." Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of "the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware."
- **MSA § 18.1** selects New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.
- **MSA § 2.3** (Order of Precedence) provides that in any conflict, "the Data Processing Addendum, then this Agreement, then the Statement of Work" applies.

**Why it matters:**

- **The DPA prevails.** Because the DPA sits at the top of the order of precedence, its Delaware clause controls over the MSA's New York clause for anything within its reach. The MSA's New York choice therefore does not protect Harrowgate on data matters.
- **The reach is wide.** It extends to any dispute "relating to" processing of end-customer data or a Security Incident.
- **Split law and forum.** Harrowgate is a New York corporation, and the Term Sheet (§ 11) called for New York law and New York County courts for all Definitive Agreements. Under the drafts, a single incident would produce claims in two places:
  - **Delaware** for the data breach claim, including notification costs under DPA § 5.5;
  - **New York** for related claims under the MSA, such as lost goods, SLA failures and indemnity.
- **Practical consequences.** Each side could file first in its preferred court. This invites parallel proceedings, inconsistent rulings and duplicated cost, and gives Bellweather a forum-shopping lever.
- **No matching jury waiver in the DPA.** The DPA has no counterpart to the MSA § 18.4 jury waiver.
- **Precedence is too broad.** The precedence clause lets the DPA override the MSA on *any* conflict, not only on data-protection substance. That is broader than necessary.

**Recommended fix:**

(a) Replace DPA § 9.1 with:

> **9.1 Governing Law and Forum.** This DPA, and any dispute arising out of or relating to it, shall be governed by the governing law and resolved in the forum specified in Section 18 of the Agreement, and Sections 18.2 through 18.4 of the Agreement apply to this DPA as if set out in full.

(b) Narrow MSA § 2.3:

> ...provided that the Data Processing Addendum shall prevail only with respect to the Processing and protection of Personal Data and Customer Data, and Section 18 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution), Section 11 (Limitation of Liability) and Section 17 (General) of this Agreement shall prevail over any conflicting provision of the Data Processing Addendum or any Statement of Work.

We should also ask Bellweather to explain why Delaware was chosen. Bellweather's state of organization is not stated in the drafts (see Part III.F). Delaware may simply be its home jurisdiction.

### Issue 4: Automatic 3-year renewals behind a 15-day opt-out window

**Where:** MSA § 14.2. Compare MSA § 14.1 and Term Sheet §§ 5 and 10.2.

**What it says:**

- After the 2-year Initial Term (January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028), the MSA "shall automatically renew for successive renewal terms of three (3) years each."
- The only exit is notice of non-renewal delivered "during the fifteen (15) day period ending one hundred twenty (120) days before the expiry" of the current term.
- "Notice of non-renewal delivered at any other time shall be of no effect."
- The MSA contains no right to terminate for convenience.

**Why it matters:**

- **The window is narrow and early.** For the Initial Term, the window is roughly mid-August to early September 2028 (exact dates to be calendared). Notice given a day early or a day late is void.
- **Renewals are long.** Each renewal is 50% longer than the Initial Term.
- **Combined effect with Issue 1.** Without the exclusivity fix, a missed window would lock Harrowgate into nationwide exclusivity for three more years.
- **SOWs follow the MSA.** SOW No. 1 continues until the MSA expires (SOW § 2.3). The fixed $184,500 monthly fee would therefore roll forward with no repricing mechanism.
- **Nothing was agreed on renewal.** The Term Sheet left renewal "to be negotiated" (§ 10.2). The 3-year auto-renewal is Bellweather's opening position, not an agreed term.
- **Statutory protection is unlikely to help.** New York General Obligations Law § 5-903 requires the service provider to give a reminder notice before an auto-renewal deadline can be enforced. It applies to certain contracts for service, maintenance or repair to or for real or personal property. Whether a logistics MSA falls within it is uncertain, and we should not rely on it.

**Recommended fix:** Replace § 14.2 with:

> **14.2 Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive renewal terms of one (1) year each (each, a "**Renewal Term**"), unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the expiry of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term. Provider shall give Customer written notice of each upcoming renewal not less than thirty (30) and not more than sixty (60) days before the last date on which Customer may give notice of non-renewal.

Also add these protections:

- **Termination for convenience.** A Customer right to terminate on 180 days' notice after the first 12 months, with any early-termination fee limited to unamortized, documented start-up costs.
- **Repricing at renewal.** A right to renegotiate Fees before any Renewal Term begins.
- **Transition assistance.** Confirmation that MSA § 15.2 transition assistance applies on non-renewal as well as termination. It appears to, but this should be made explicit.

## III. Secondary Issues

### A. Liability cap is ambiguous and leaves data incidents capped

**Where:** MSA § 11.1; DPA § 5.5.

**The problem:**

- **Ambiguous measure.** The cap, "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim," does not say whose fees, under which SOW, or whether "claim" means the event or the demand. A claim in the first months of the relationship would be capped at a very small amount.
- **Data incident costs capped.** Bellweather's obligation to reimburse Security Incident costs under DPA § 5.5 (notification, call center, credit monitoring) arises under the "Agreement" because the DPA forms part of it. Those costs therefore fall under the general cap.
- **Loss and damage to goods capped.** Bellweather's landed-cost liability for lost or damaged goods (MSA § 6.3, SOW § 6.3) is also capped. This is unusual for warehouse custody.

**Recommended fix:**

- Reword the cap as: "the greater of (a) the total Fees paid and payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Statements of Work in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim, and (b) $2,214,000."
- Add a separate super-cap for Bellweather's data-protection breaches and Security Incidents. For example, the greater of 3x annual Fees or the $3M cyber limit.
- Carve loss of or damage to Customer Goods out of the cap, or cap it at no less than the $5M warehouse legal liability limit.

### B. Bellweather's indemnity omits data and goods

**Where:** MSA § 10.1.

**The problem:** Bellweather's indemnity does not cover third-party claims arising from Security Incidents or breach of the DPA. It also does not cover end-customer claims arising from delivery failures by Bellweather personnel, other than bodily injury and property damage.

**Recommended fix:** Add indemnities for:

- Bellweather's breach of § 8, § 9 or the DPA; and
- any claim by end customers arising from the acts or omissions of Bellweather personnel in their residences.

### C. Insurance: the Quillmore letter is informational only

**Where:** Quillmore cover letter §§ 3–5; MSA § 12.

**Assessment:**

- **Limits.** The letter reports limits that match MSA § 12.1. On its face, no limit is deficient.
- **Not a contract term.** The letter is a broker's informational letter. It does not change the negotiation and should not be treated as satisfying any contractual requirement. The letter itself says the Certificate "does not amend, extend or alter" coverage (§ 5.1).
- **Endorsements still pending.** The additional-insured endorsements are not yet issued. They are promised "on execution of the Agreement" (§ 3.1).
- **Policy expiry mid-year.** The policies expire July 1, 2027, six months into the relationship.
- **Claims-made cyber cover.** The cyber policy is written on a claims-made basis.
- **Coverage gap against our proposed changes.** If we narrow Harrowgate's indemnity and expand Bellweather's, Bellweather's coverage should respond. Currently Harrowgate is only an additional insured on the CGL and auto policies.

**Recommended fix:**

- Require copies of the actual AI endorsements before the Start Date, on a primary and non-contributory basis with waiver of subrogation.
- Add Harrowgate as loss payee on warehouse legal liability and cargo coverage.
- Require a 3-year tail or extended reporting period for the claims-made cyber policy.
- Consider increasing cargo limits above $250,000 per vehicle, given white-glove furniture loads.

### D. Unilateral control of indemnified claims

**Where:** MSA § 10.3.

**The problem:** The indemnifying party gets "sole control" of the defense. Given the breadth of § 10.2, Bellweather could steer defense strategy on claims involving Harrowgate's brand and end customers.

**Recommended fix:** Add a right for the indemnified party to assume its own defense, at the indemnitor's cost, where there is a conflict of interest. Also add a consent right over any settlement involving Harrowgate's end customers.

### E. Force majeure exclusivity relief

**Where:** MSA § 17.2.

**The problem:** Substitute services are permitted only after 15 days, and only "for the duration of the event."

**Recommended fix:** Tie this to the exclusivity carve-out proposed in Issue 1. Add a termination right if a force majeure event continues for more than 30 days.

### F. Provider's identity and organization

**Where:** MSA preamble.

**The problem:** The preamble does not state Bellweather's state of organization. This is relevant to Issue 3 and to the § 16.1 representation.

**Recommended fix:** Request that Bellweather fill in its state of organization.

### G. Subprocessor annex is blank

**Where:** DPA Annex 3.

**The problem:** The annex is to be completed before the Start Date, but no subprocessors have been listed.

**Recommended fix:** Request the list now, so Harrowgate can vet it before signing.
